name: MX25R3235FM1IL0
title: MX25R3235F 32 Mbit wide-supply serial NOR flash with single, dual and quad I/O
summary: MX25R3235F is a 32 Mbit (4 MB, organised 4,194,304 x 8) serial NOR flash that reads, programs and erases from one supply anywhere between 1.65 V and 3.6 V. It talks SPI in mode 0 or mode 3 and widens to two or four data lines for reads and for quad page programming. A volatile configuration bit picks between an Ultra Low Power mode (5 uA typical standby, 33 MHz single-line reads) and a High Performance mode (80 MHz on one, two or four lines). MX25R3235FM1IL0 is the 8-pin 150 mil SOP part with a RESET# pin that starts in Ultra Low Power mode.
key_figures: 5 uA typ (Ultra Low Power), 9 uA typ (High Performance)
4 KB sector, 32 KB and 64 KB block, whole chip

operation.text: Bit 1 of configuration register-2 (L/H switch) chooses between Ultra Low Power (0) and High Performance (1). The bit is volatile, so after power-up or reset the part returns to the mode its option letter names: L parts start in Ultra Low Power, H parts in High Performance. Changing the bit is a WRSR whose self-timed cycle is tWMS (20 us max), and that WRSR must be clocked at 33 MHz or less. Execute-in-place (performance enhance) works only in High Performance mode.

SPI mode 0 and mode 3 are both accepted: the part latches input on SCLK rising edges and drives output after falling edges. A command is a one-byte code, most significant bit first, followed by a 3-byte address where needed. Read-type commands (RDID, RDSR, RDCR, RDSCUR, the reads, RDSFDP, RES, REMS) may be ended by raising CS# after any output bit. Commands that change state (WREN, WRDI, WRSR, the erases and programs, DP, ENSO, EXSO, WRSCUR, RST, RSTEN, NOP, suspend and resume) run only if CS# rises exactly on a byte boundary. An unknown code puts the part in standby with SO floating until the next CS# fall. While a write, program or erase runs, array reads are ignored and do not disturb it.

READ (03h) runs to fR, 33 MHz, with no dummy cycles. FAST_READ (0Bh) adds 8 dummy cycles and runs to fC. DREAD (3Bh) and QREAD (6Bh) take the address on SI and return data on two or four lines after 8 dummy cycles. 2READ (BBh) sends address and data on two lines with 4 dummy cycles; 4READ (EBh) sends them on four lines with 6 (2 mode cycles plus 4). The DC bit of configuration register-1 lengthens these to 8 and 10. In every read the address advances by itself and wraps from the top of the array to 0, so one command can read the whole chip. 4READ and 4PP need the QE bit set first. In Ultra Low Power mode 4READ may run at 16 MHz if it stays within one 4 Mbit bank; crossing a bank needs a fresh command. During 2READ the first two dummy cycles must hold 0h or Fh on each line.

In 4READ the two cycles after the address carry a mode byte P[7:0]. If each upper nibble bit is the inverse of the lower one (A5h, 5Ah, F0h, 0Fh) the part stays in read mode after CS# rises and takes the next CS# fall as the start of an address, skipping the command byte. A mode byte without that toggle (FFh, 00h, AAh, 55h) followed by a CS# cycle, or the command FFh, leaves the mode. Dual I/O reads do not support it. A resume command is ignored while the part is in this mode.

SBL (C0h) followed by one data byte sets wrap-around: 00h to 03h wrap within 8, 16, 32 or 64 bytes inside the 256-byte page from any start address; 1xh turns wrapping off. Wrap is off after power-up and stays as set until power is removed or the part is reset. 4READ (EBh) follows the wrap setting.

PP (02h) and 4PP (38h) program bits from 1 to 0 within one 256-byte page and need WEL set by WREN first. The low address byte picks where writing begins; data running past the end of a page wraps to its first byte, and if more than 256 bytes arrive only the last 256 are kept. Programming starts when CS# rises on a byte boundary and lasts tPP; WIP reads 1 throughout and WEL clears at the end. A page must be erased before it is programmed. A page inside the BP-protected area is not programmed.

SE (20h), BE32K (52h) and BE (D8h) take any address inside the 4 KB sector, 32 KB block or 64 KB block to erase to all ones; CE (60h or C7h) erases the whole array and runs only when BP3-BP0 are all 0. Each needs WEL set, starts when CS# rises on the byte boundary after the last address bit, and reports progress through WIP; WEL clears when it ends. A protected sector or block is left unchanged.

operation.topic: Write enable latch and status polling
operation.text: WREN (06h) sets WEL, which must be 1 before any program, erase, WRSR or WRSCUR. WEL clears at power-up, on RESET# low, on WRDI, at the end of each of those operations, on a suspend, and after a software reset. A program or erase aimed at a protected area is dropped and also clears WEL. RDSR can be issued at any time, even during an operation; poll until WIP is 0, then check WEL is 0. The P_FAIL and E_FAIL bits of the security register report whether the last program or erase failed or hit a protected region, and clear on the next success.

WRSR (01h) writes one, two or three bytes: the status register, then configuration register-1, then configuration register-2; CS# must rise after 8, 16 or 24 data bits or the command is dropped. The self-timed cycle is tW. WRSR cannot change WEL or WIP, and is refused in hardware protected mode.

BP3-BP0 in the status register protect from 1 to all 64 of the 64 KB blocks against program and erase, counted from the top of the array, or from the bottom once the one-time-programmable TB bit is set to 1. All BP bits are 0 when shipped. With SRWD at 1 and WP# low the part is in hardware protected mode: SRWD and the BP bits become read-only until WP# goes high again. With WP# held high permanently only software protection applies. Setting QE to 1 for quad operation turns off the WP# and RESET#/HOLD# functions, and with them hardware protection.

An extra 8 Kbit one-time-programmable area sits outside the main array in two 4 Kbit halves: xxx000-xxx1FF for the customer and xxx200-xxx3FF for the factory. ENSO (B1h) switches reads and programs to this area and EXSO (C1h) switches back; the main array cannot be reached meanwhile, and WRSR and WRSCUR are refused. WRSCUR sets LDSO to lock the customer half for good; bit 0 of the security register shows whether the factory half is locked. A unique ID is offered.

Suspend (75h or B0h) pauses a page program or a sector or block erase so the rest of the array can be read. After tPSL or tESL, WEL clears and PSB or ESB in the security register goes to 1; then the reads and other commands in the suspend tables are accepted. During an erase suspend a page may be programmed anywhere unprotected outside the suspended sector or block, and that program cannot itself be suspended. Resume (7Ah or 30h) sets WEL and WIP again and clears PSB or ESB; wait tPRS or tERS before the next suspend, and allow at least 100 us (program) or 280 us (erase) per resume-to-suspend loop for the operation to progress.

RSTEN (66h) then RST (99h) returns the part to standby with every volatile bit and setting at its power-on value. Any other command between the two cancels the reset; NOP (00h) cancels a pending RSTEN. A reset during program or erase aborts it and the data being written may be lost. Recovery takes tREADY2, longest after a program or erase.

On RESET# parts, holding RESET# low for at least tRLRH resets the part to standby with volatile bits at their power-on values; SO floats and current drops to a minimum while it is low. A program or erase in progress is aborted and its data may be lost. CS# may go low tRHSL after RESET# rises, and the part is ready after tREADY1 or tREADY2.

On HOLD# parts, HOLD# low with CS# low pauses the serial transfer without deselecting the part; the pause starts and ends at the next SCLK-low moment after HOLD# falls or rises. SO floats and SI is ignored meanwhile. A program, erase or status write already running continues. Raising CS# during a hold resets the interface logic. HOLD is not available in quad I/O mode.
WP#/SIO2 and RESET#/SIO3 (or HOLD#/SIO3) have internal pull-ups that act while the pin is not connected in the system; connecting the pin to anything turns the pull-up off.

DP (B9h) moves the part from standby (ISB1) to deep power-down (ISB2) within tDP after CS# rises; it then ignores all commands. After at least tDPDD in that state, a CS# low pulse of tCRDP, a hardware reset or a power cycle wakes it, and it is back in standby tRDP after CS# rises. The power-on state is standby, not deep power-down.

With VCC between its minimum and 2.0 V, holding WP#/SIO2 at 7 V to 8 V throughout a program or erase shortens it (the Vhv rows of the timing tables). CS# may go low only after tVSL1 + tVhv + tVhv2, WP# must stay at Vhv until WIP shows the operation done, and if Vhv sags the operation may fail.

Below VWI the internal logic is held reset and commands are ignored. The part must not be selected until VCC has reached its minimum and a further tVSL (800 us) has passed; reads, writes, programs and erases are all accepted after that. CS# should track VCC during power-up and power-down, and a pull-up on CS# helps. For a clean restart VCC must fall below VPWD for at least tPWD. A write, program or erase interrupted by VCC falling below VWI may corrupt data. A capacitor of about 0.1 uF next to the package pins steadies VCC.
Power-on reset, a check that each command ends on a byte boundary, the WREN requirement, deep power-down and the block-protect bits guard against accidental writes from supply transitions or noise.
The array ships erased, every byte FFh, and the status register reads 00h.

RDID (9Fh) returns C2h (Macronix), memory type 28h and density 16h. RES (ABh) after three dummy bytes returns the electronic ID 16h, repeating while clocked; it is kept for older designs. REMS (90h) after two dummy bytes and an address byte returns C2h and 16h, in the order the address picks, alternating while clocked. RDID is not decoded during a program or erase. RDSFDP (5Ah) reads the JEDEC JESD216B parameter tables like FAST_READ, with 8 dummy cycles.
The part endures at least 100,000 erase/program cycles and keeps data for 20 years. Latch-up is protected to 100 mA from -1 V to VCC + 1 V. All packages are RoHS compliant and halogen-free.
The WSON and USON packages have a metal pad underneath. It may float or join the GND pin's ground and must not go to any other net; keep vias and traces out from under it.
